title: Longest Consecutive Sequence in an Array
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Length of the longest run of consecutive integers present in the array (order irrelevant).
intuition: Only start counting from numbers that begin a run — those with no x-1 in the set. That single guard is what keeps the total work linear despite the inner while loop.

approaches.title: Brute: sort then scan
approaches.idea: Sorting makes runs adjacent; skip duplicates.
limitations: Perfectly acceptable if O(n) is not demanded

approaches.title: Optimal: hash set, count only from run starts
approaches.idea: For each x with no x-1, walk x+1, x+2, ... upward.
approaches.dryRun:
s={100,4,200,1,3,2}
x=1 is a start -> 1,2,3,4 length 4
x=100 start -> length 1
x=200 start -> length 1
best 4
approaches.whyWorks: Each run is walked exactly once, from its smallest element, so total inner work is O(n).

edgeCases: Duplicates must not inflate the run
commonMistakes: Dropping the `x - 1 in s` guard, turning the algorithm into O(n^2)
Using a list instead of a set (membership becomes O(n))
patternRecognition: "Consecutive values, any order" -> hash set with run-start pruning
followUps: Longest consecutive path in a binary tree
interviewInsight: Be ready to argue the amortised bound out loud — the nested while loop looks quadratic until you explain the guard.
